content:
The [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Convert km/L, L/100km, US MPG and UK MPG with the correct reciprocal relationship. Enter your fuel economy or consumption and input unit and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Fuel economy is expressed as distance per unit of fuel in some markets and fuel per unit of distance in others. Because these are reciprocal measures, higher MPG or km/L means better efficiency while higher L/100km means greater consumption. This converter handles US and imperial gallons separately and adds the fuel required for a 1,000 km journey. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Fuel Economy Converter

Start by entering your fuel economy or consumption, then choosing your input unit from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the vehicle figure and select exactly which unit the source uses.
2. Compare the desired output, taking care to distinguish US MPG from UK MPG.
3. For real trip estimates, use fuel consumed and distance travelled under comparable driving conditions rather than only a laboratory rating.

## Formula

km/L = 100 ÷ (L/100km). US MPG = km/L × 2.352145833. UK MPG = km/L × 2.824809363. L/100km = 100 ÷ km/L.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 30 US MPG is about 12.754 km/L, 7.841 L/100km or 36.034 UK MPG. At that consumption, a 1,000 km journey uses approximately 78.406 litres. Try the same figures in the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Fuel economy or consumption: 30, Input unit: US miles per gallon), the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) returns Kilometres per litre: 12.75431 km/L, Litres per 100 km: 7.84049 L/100km, US miles per gallon: 30 MPG, UK miles per gallon: 36.0285 MPG, Fuel used per 1,000 km: 78.405 L. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Temperature Converter](/temperature-converter) is worth a look before you finish.

## Why the conversion is not a simple multiplier

Converting MPG to L/100km requires both unit conversion and inversion. Thirty US MPG does not equal thirty times a fixed L/100km factor; it is 235.214583 ÷ 30, or about 7.84 L/100km. Similarly, moving from 10 to 5 L/100km halves fuel use, while moving from 10 to 5 km/L doubles it.

## US and imperial gallons differ

A US liquid gallon is 3.785411784 litres, whereas an imperial gallon is 4.54609 litres. The same vehicle therefore has a larger numerical UK MPG than US MPG. Never compare official economy figures without checking the gallon standard and the underlying test cycle.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Lower L/100km is better; higher MPG and km/L are better.
- Confirm whether an advertised MPG figure uses US or imperial gallons.
- Weather, load, tyres, speed and congestion can make real consumption differ from test figures.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I convert US MPG to L/100km?

Divide 235.214583 by the US MPG value. For example, 30 MPG converts to approximately 7.841 L/100km. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Why is UK MPG higher than US MPG?

The imperial gallon is larger, so a vehicle can travel more miles per imperial gallon than per US gallon at the same actual efficiency. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is fuel economy the same as fuel consumption?

They describe reciprocal quantities. Economy is distance per fuel amount; consumption is fuel amount per distance. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Fuel Economy Converter use?

km/L = 100 ÷ (L/100km). US MPG = km/L × 2.352145833. UK MPG = km/L × 2.824809363. L/100km = 100 ÷ km/L. You can see it in action in the [Fuel Economy Converter](/fuel-economy-converter) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
